collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager unwraps the half-built canoe they started long ago: finish it at last, or give it to someone else.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Under (subject)'s hut, wrapped in palm leaves, is a canoe (subject.he/she) started building a very long time ago. It's half finished. The hull is shaped, but there's no outrigger, no seat, no paint. Every year, (subject.he/she) means to get back to it. Today, looking for a lost basket, (subject.he/she) unwraps it for the first time in years.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) decides that this is the year. It takes all season, mostly in evenings. Some of the wood has to be replaced. Some of (subject.his/her) old work, (subject.he/she) realizes, wasn't very good, and (subject.he/she) redoes it. When it's finally done, (subject.he/she) paddles it out past the reef, alone, at dawn. It's a good canoe. It's taken half (subject.his/her) life. (subject.He/she) decides that's not too long for a good canoe.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) looks at it for a long time and realizes (subject.he/she) doesn't want to finish it. (subject.He/she) wanted to want to finish it. That's different. (subject.He/she) gives it to (young_villager), a young villager who's been wanting a canoe of (young_villager.his/her) own. (young_villager) finishes it in a month, slightly badly, and paddles out grinning. (subject) watches from the beach and feels lighter than (subject.he/she) has in years.
